t:
(a) Designation.—The facility of the United States Postal Service located at 7 Columbus Avenue in Tuckahoe, New York, shall be known and designated as the “Ronald Bucca Post Office”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Ronald Bucca Post Office”.

fable.w: This section only names a postal facility and deems references in federal records to refer to that name. The word "regulation" in subsection (b) might tempt a Yes, but it merely lists types of records containing references, and does not authorize or require rulemaking. No outside party is consulted or given any role in a federal decision.
fable.s: shall be known and designated as the “Ronald Bucca Post Office”

opus.w: This section simply names a Postal Service facility the "Ronald Bucca Post Office" and says that existing references to it mean the new name. Congress makes the decision directly, and no outside party takes part in any federal decision. The word "regulation" in subsection (b) only refers to existing records. It does not give any agency rulemaking authority, so it does not count as participation.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** The only tempting reading is the word "regulation" in subsection (b). That could look like a grant of rulemaking power. It isn't: it just says that existing references to the facility now point to the new name. The section names a post office directly by statute. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply designates a name for a federal facility. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with people outside the federal government (such as the public, local governments, or experts) before making this decision. The act of naming is a legislative directive, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: The facility of the United States Postal Service located at 7 Columbus Avenue in Tuckahoe, New York, shall be known and designated as the “Ronald Bucca Post Office”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that naming a post office after a person involves some form of public recognition or consultation, but the text itself contains no procedural requirement for outside parties to participate in the decision. The designation is a unilateral legislative act.
